_comment: Dataset V2 task §26 - predeclared BEFORE launching the one permitted QLoRA training run, and before any HF_QLORA_V2 metric of any kind has been observed. Only HF_BASE_V2 (no adapter) exists at declare time.
declaredBeforeSeeing: HF_QLORA_V2 - training has not started; only HF_BASE_V2 (71-case validation, no adapter) exists

unsafeOutputRate.note: base.unsafeOutputRate = 0.0 after fixing a real false-positive in unsafe_output()'s UNSAFE_MARKERS (the generic 'UPDATE ' marker matched the ordinary word 'update' in unrelated text - see qwen4b-baseline-experiment-v2.md). Any genuinely unsafe output in QLoRA is disqualifying regardless of this gate.

jsonValidityRate.note: D1's core finding was QLoRA degenerating into non-JSON prose/repetition loops far more than base (71% vs 19% token-ceiling hits). If V2 training doesn't fix this, it must show up here as a hard fail, not get buried under an improved invented-enum number.

schemaValidityRate.note: Same bar as V1's gate (task §26: 'must materially improve if ontology training works'). base.schemaValidityRate = 0.0 (HF_BASE_V2), so this requires qlora.schemaValidityRate >= 0.15 in absolute terms.

primaryIntentAccuracy.note: Soft gate per task §26 ('must improve meaningfully' interpreted as the same +0.15 bar as V1, but non-fatal alone since schemaValidityRate is the harder, more direct signal).

entityF1Mean.note: D1's finding: entity extraction regressed under QLoRA (0.429->0.333 in D1's 21-case set). V2 added explicit entity+intent co-occurrence families specifically to fix this - must show up here, not just in the dataset design.

correctionAccuracy.comparison: (base.correctionAccuracy is None) or (qlora.correctionAccuracy is None) or (base.correctionAccuracy - qlora.correctionAccuracy <= 0.10)
correctionAccuracy.note: Only evaluated over cases where correction is applicable (evaluate_semantics.py's None-for-not-applicable convention).

referenceAccuracy.comparison: (base.referenceAccuracy is None) or (qlora.referenceAccuracy is None) or (base.referenceAccuracy - qlora.referenceAccuracy <= 0.10)
referenceAccuracy.note: Same reasoning as correctionAccuracy. base.referenceAccuracy = 0.0 on HF_BASE_V2, so this gate cannot fail from a floor effect - a genuine new regression below zero is impossible; a real test is whether QLoRA manages to rise above 0.

ambiguityAccuracy.note: Task §13's first-class ambiguity/UNKNOWN discipline requirement - a model that forces every ambiguous utterance into a confident intent is a regression even if other metrics improve.

inventedEnumRate.note: D1's critical finding: this number improving is NOT sufficient evidence of learned ontology if it's really a jsonValidityRate side effect (an unparseable output can't be flagged invented-enum). This gate is informational only - the real check is the manual enum-fix intersection analysis (task §32), done by hand against jsonValidityRate's gate above, not trusted alone.

maxTokenHitRate.note: D1's single cleanest signal of degeneration (19%->71% in the old adapter). If V2's adapter still frequently hits the 160-token ceiling, that is itself disqualifying regardless of any other metric improving.

manualGatesNotAutomaticallyEvaluated._comment: task §26's NON_JSON_FORMAT-dominance and generation-degeneration checks are not in evaluate_semantics.py's standard errorBucketCounts (by design - task §23 says reuse, do not redesign, the evaluator). These are checked by hand using the same post-hoc taxonomy method as D1 (classify each invalid-JSON case into TRUNCATED_AT_TOKEN_LIMIT / MALFORMED_JSON_SYNTAX / NON_JSON_FORMAT / REPEATED_JSON_OR_CONTENT / EMPTY_OUTPUT from rawText), reported in qwen4b-baseline-experiment-v2.md before the final verdict is written - not mechanically gated here, but just as binding on the final QLORA_SIGNAL decision.
manualGatesNotAutomaticallyEvaluated.nonJsonFormatDominance: NON_JSON_FORMAT must not be the plurality invalid-JSON category for HF_QLORA_V2 the way it was for the old adapter (12/14 = 86% of invalid cases in D1).
manualGatesNotAutomaticallyEvaluated.generationDegeneration: REPEATED_JSON_OR_CONTENT (verbatim repetition loops) count for HF_QLORA_V2 must not exceed HF_BASE_V2's count by a wide margin - any repetition-loop case at all is a degeneration signal worth flagging even if the gate above (maxTokenHitRate) happens to pass.

overallDecisionRule: QLORA_MEANINGFULLY_IMPROVED only if: no hard gate fails, AND schemaValidityRate gate passes, AND the manual NON_JSON_FORMAT/degeneration checks show real improvement over the old adapter's degeneration pattern. QLORA_SMALL_IMPROVEMENT if hard gates pass but deltas are smaller than the thresholds above, or if schemaValidityRate improves but degeneration is only partially fixed. QLORA_NO_IMPROVEMENT if no hard gate fails but nothing materially improves either. QLORA_REGRESSED if any must_not_worsen/must_not_materially_regress/must_not_materially_increase gate fails. Matches evaluate_semantics.py's --backend hf invocation exactly as used for HF_BASE_V2 (same max_new_tokens=160/do_sample=False/timeout=100) for HF_QLORA_V2, so this is apples-to-apples per D1's own corrective methodology.
